title: Say what the pre-push hook is doing while git push waits on it
body:
With sync set up, git push goes quiet for several seconds before anything appears. That is the pre-push hook running foam sync, which makes three round trips to origin in a row, ls-remote, fetch and push, every one with --quiet, and prints its one line only after each has finished. Someone used to git push returning at once reads the silence as a hang.

Print a line to stderr before each network step so the wait has a name: foam: syncing refs/foam/data with origin, then fetched, merged, pushed as they happen, and nothing at all when there is nothing to move. The hook runs in the person's terminal, so stderr reaches them.

Also worth trimming the wait itself: skip ls-remote when the local ref already knows the remote's tip, and skip the push when the local ref is not ahead of what the last fetch brought in. Each round trip saved is time git push gets back.

git pull has no foam hook. The fetch refspec rides the same connection as the branches, so a slow pull is more likely the remote than foam; check with GIT_TRACE=1 before blaming the refspec.
close_reason: sync names each round trip before it starts, skips the push when origin has the tip, and drops the ls-remote; hook test checks stderr

notes.author: Jack Roddy/6de6737a
notes.text: Done in the working tree. sync prints 'foam: syncing' before the fetch and 'foam: pushing' before the push on stderr; result lines go to stdout by hand and to stderr with a foam: prefix under the hook, since git sends a hook's stdout to stderr anyway. ls-remote is gone from sync: fetch_if_present treats git's 'couldn't find remote ref' as no ref, the same string-matching push() already does. The push is skipped when refs/foam/origin equals refs/foam/data after the merge. git pull was not touched: it has no hook.
